# Issue 69 — Independent proactive visual QA

[Issue #69: Check the current device microphone without creating a project take](https://github.com/dystrophyless/dubbed.ai/issues/69)

Reviewer: **GPT-6.1 Sol, High**. Review date: **2026-10-25**. This reviewer owns only issue 69. Review only; no fixes, issue changes, commits, publication or acceptance decision.

## Verdict and evidence boundary

**Two MEDIUM requirement/design flaws and one LOW confirmed implementation defect. No HIGH finding.** The bounded fake-device journey works, including explicit connection, optional test/Stop, local keyboard playback, retry, clean exit and disabled continuation after denial/loss. Its main usability weakness is that compact desktop actions and the position of the ready Continue action make a simple readiness check feel more laborious than necessary.

Code: `9d286621177200fdb5f61ef963d0b6818ae76774`, local mock Vite 8.3.5 on isolated port 4369. Installed Chromium **156.0.8078.4**, Windows, headless, DPR 1; screenshots use normal CSS pixels. The browser was launched with `--mute-audio --use-fake-device-for-media-stream --use-fake-ui-for-media-stream`; every media element was also muted with volume zero. **No physical microphone or speaker was used.** Native browser permission chrome and real hardware behavior are not established.

The issue snapshot in `../contracts/issue-69.md` is dated 2026-10-25, closed, with zero discussion comments. Active local Flow 09, shared decisions, current tokens, adoption workflow and catalog govern this review; historical publication hashes are provenance. Existing unrelated dirty docs, skills and older evidence were preserved. `git diff --name-only -- frontend` was empty before finalization and HEAD remained the baseline above. Only this issue's disposable scripts, report and evidence remain from the review. Vite was terminated through its owned process handle.

The user job is: choose a usable current-device input, understand whether it is connected, optionally hear a short private test, then continue without creating a take or paying credits. The optional test must remain optional in both behavior and presentation.

## Executed procedure

Commands: `node frontend/node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js --mode mock --host 127.0.0.1 --port 4369 --strictPort` from `frontend`; `node issue-69/capture.cjs` and `node issue-69/supplement.cjs` using their actual repository evidence paths. Raw console logs are `capture.log` and `supplement.log`; raw geometry, fonts, text and lifecycle observations are `metrics.json` and `supplement-metrics.json`.

Registration and verification used the visible UI and its explicitly labelled local mock code. The microphone route was opened directly as `/microphone?origin=new`; this does not prove the project-origin first-recording redirect. Locale changes used the visible desktop language selector, restoring each target viewport before capture; the mobile navigation locale control itself was not audited.

Fault injection is isolated to the disposable browser realm: `getUserMedia` rejects with `NotAllowedError` only when explicitly toggled; a real fake-device track receives a synthetic `ended` event; `MediaRecorder.start` temporarily throws `NotSupportedError`; an audio element receives a synthetic error event; and `enumerateDevices` temporarily rejects. These prove screen handling and recovery, not native denial/revocation, unplugging, codec support or OS contention.

All **27 review screenshots were opened and visually inspected** with `view_image`. `screenshot-manifest.json` records each filename, viewport, full-page versus viewport capture, SHA-256 and inspection flag. Six EN/RU entry and six EN/RU ready captures cover 1440×900, 1440×700 and 390×844. RU ready also covers 767 and 768 widths. Further captures cover testing, playback, keyboard/native focus, denial, retry, loss, test/playback/enumeration failure and exact short/phone viewport crops.

## Expected versus observed

| Contract/state | Expected | Actual fresh observation | Result/evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| AC-01: explicit permission, no automatic test/take | Entry must not start capture | Before connection: 0 getUserMedia calls, 0 recorder starts, no audio element | Confirmed at direct route; `entry-en-desktop.png`, `entry-ru-phone.png`; project redirect remains untested |
| AC-02: usable input and readiness-only Continue | Browser-exposed list; explicit connect; test not mandatory | Chromium fake-device inputs are displayed honestly as Fake inputs. Continue enabled after connection before any test. Meter carries name/min/max/current numeric semantics | Confirmed fake-device boundary; `ready-en-desktop.png`, `ready-ru-phone.png`; no real-device claim |
| AC-03: temporary Record/Stop/Listen | Local test bytes; cleanup on leave; no project take | Record/Stop yields Blob URL. Tab from Record then Space on native audio starts playback: focused=true, paused=false, currentTime>0, muted=true, volume=0. Leave stops track, revokes 1 of 1 created Blob URLs; IDB writes unchanged at 26 before/after leave; return has no audio | Confirmed bounded lifecycle; `testing-en-desktop.png`, `playback-en-desktop.png`, metrics checks. No exhaustive service mutation spy or active-test exit in this fresh run |
| AC-04: denied/lost input | Truthful recovery and disabled Continue | Denial/loss disable Continue; explicit retry connects. Denial also retains contradictory initial status, QA-69-03 | Partial; `denied-en-desktop.png`, `denied-ru-phone.png`, `retry-ready-ru-phone.png`, `lost-ru-phone.png` |
| AC-04: enumeration/test/playback failure | Distinct truthful states; usable default and retry | Enumeration failure says default can be tried; connecting default enables Continue. Recorder failure is local to test; restoring recorder and retry yields audio. Playback error text is shown without blocking readiness | Confirmed injected handling only; `enumeration-failed-en-desktop.png`, `test-failed-en-desktop.png`, `playback-failed-en-desktop.png`, supplement checks |
| AC-05: localization, responsive, keyboard | EN/RU layout; phone targets; meaningful level/status; keyboard controls | No page horizontal overflow in all 27 captures. Phone buttons/select are 48px with 16px labels. Desktop button targets are 24/28/32px with 12/13px labels. Native audio keyboard operation works; native focus outline visible on phone playback | Bounded pass with QA-69-01/02 design criticism; no screen-reader or forced-color acceptance |
| AC-VIS-01: Clean/Light mapping and Mabry | Reference treatment and documented media derivatives | Mabry Pro 400/500 loaded. Neutral white/black controls, thin Lucide outlines, quiet panel rules, source button sizing and 4px PGR-derived meter are recognizable. Input/native audio are derivatives, not fabricated library components | Bounded visual comparison. No claim of pixel-perfect full-state fidelity or completed motion/zoom/device acceptance |

## Findings

### QA-69-01 — MEDIUM — Desktop setup and recovery controls are unnecessarily small

**Class:** requirement/design flaw, confirmed geometry; follows the selected density rather than violating it. **Affected:** AC-05, AC-VIS-01; desktop token density and Flow 09 device setup/recovery.

**Reproduce:** Open the check at 1440×900, grant the fake-device connection, inspect Refresh devices, Connect selected microphone, Record test/Stop and Continue. Repeat at width 768: targets shrink abruptly from phone sizing.

**Expected quality:** A dedicated device setup screen should offer easy-to-read, easy-to-point-to actions, particularly recovery and Stop. **Actual:** Refresh is **24px high with 12px/16px text**; Connect and Record test/Stop are **28px with 13px/20px text**; Continue is **32px with 13px/20px text**. The select is 40px with 16px text. Several 670px-wide action rows still have only 28px vertical targets, producing a visibly thin strip and small labels inside an otherwise spacious 720px panel. Phone targets correctly reach 48px, but 768px immediately receives the compact desktop treatment.

Measured evidence is in `metrics.json`, ready desktop and 767/768 observations. Source: [MicrophoneScreen.tsx:338](D:/Program/python/Dubbed/frontend/src/features/microphone/MicrophoneScreen.tsx:338), [MicrophoneScreen.tsx:367](D:/Program/python/Dubbed/frontend/src/features/microphone/MicrophoneScreen.tsx:367), [MicrophoneScreen.tsx:410](D:/Program/python/Dubbed/frontend/src/features/microphone/MicrophoneScreen.tsx:410); approved [design-tokens.md:88](D:/Program/python/Dubbed/_docs/frontend-flows/design-tokens.md:88) explicitly specifies 24/28/32 desktop density. Thus this is a critique of an approved requirement, **not a claim that a 24px target automatically violates accessibility**.

**Impact:** More precise pointer movement and harder reading during an already unfamiliar permission/device recovery task, without a dense-data justification for the compression. Full-width Connect makes horizontal targeting generous but does not address label size or the small vertical target.

**Recommendation:** Make a scoped, explicit device-setup adaptation: approximately 36–40px desktop action height with at least 14px labels, retaining selected colors, corner treatment, typography family and states; prioritize Connect, Stop and Continue. ### QA-69-03 — LOW — Denial retains the false initial permission status

**Class:** confirmed implementation defect. **Affected:** AC-04 truthful denial/recovery and AC-05 status meaning/localized error placement.

**Reproduce:** In an isolated browser realm, make the next `getUserMedia` call reject with `NotAllowedError`; click Allow microphone access. This injected failure crosses the actual adapter/error path; it is not evidence of native permission chrome.

**Expected:** A single coherent current state, e.g. access denied with browser-settings recovery, without claiming permission was never requested. **Actual:** the screen simultaneously displays **“Your browser has not been asked for microphone access yet.”** and **“Microphone access was denied. Allow access in your browser settings, then try again.”** RU has the same contradiction. **Impact:** Contradictory feedback during a common recovery path weakens confidence about whether access was requested and what the user should do next.

**Recommendation:** Suppress the initial waiting sentence when a current connection error exists, or give denied/error its own coherent connection status. Preserve explicit retry and disabled continuation. **Next validation:** EN/RU denial followed by successful retry; assert the initial waiting sentence disappears after failure and returns only on a genuine fresh visit.
